title: Slimline runbook adapter and ops telemetry facade
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight adapter that converts existing runbooks into 'slimline' executable tasks (slimlets) and a telemetry facade that normalizes and de-noises runbook telemetry for the Console. Goals: reduce alert/metric cardinality from ad-hoc runbook steps, provide deterministic replay metadata for dry-runs, and expose a small set of actionable signals (start/complete/error/retry/permission-fail).

Motivation and scope: Current runbooks emit heterogeneous logs/events at varying schema quality which makes it hard to create meaningful runbook-level SLOs and causes dashboard noise. The adapter will: 1) map canonical runbook step types to typed slimlets (shell, http, query, artifact-transfer, patch); 2) inject a uniform context header (runbook_id, run_id, step_id, trace_id, user_id, perms_snapshot) that persists into any outbound call; 3) produce a standardized minimal event stream consumed by the telemetry facade. The facade will perform sampling, schema validation, enrichment (geo/region, capacity tier, executor-type), aggregation (per-runbook and per-step histograms), and export to the Console telemetry store and APM traces.

Design constraints and choices: We decided to keep slimlets intentionally minimal (no heavy DSL). Each slimlet is an idempotent unit that can be executed in normal or dry-run mode. We purposefully avoid adding a full runtime language to reduce security surface and speed adoption. Telemetry will enforce an event schema v1 with semantic enums to avoid free-text status fields. For privacy/compliance, PII is redacted by the adapter before events leave the private control plane.

Interfaces and integration points: Adapter REST API for converting canonical runbooks (POST /v1/adapter/convert), an infra shim for the admin CLI to call slimlets, and a small sidecar library (Go/Python) for executors to emit the canonical context header. Telemetry facade exposes: metrics (Prometheus-compatible), events (Console store), and a trace link to APM.

Rollout plan: 1) alpha: internal-only conversion of 5 non-sensitive runbooks with dry-run (2 weeks) 2) beta: enable sampled realtime telemetry for ops teams (2 weeks) 3) canary: 5% of runbook executions enabled with auto-fallback (2 weeks) 4) GA: rollout to all internal runbooks after 6 weeks and add a migration guide for partners.

Safety and security: Every slimlet invocation requires a permission snapshot check; privileged slimlets will require an allowlist. Dry-run always executes without side-effects and produces full telemetry to validate mapping. Security review is required for the sidecar library and the adapter conversion endpoint.

Observability and SLOs: New metrics to track: runlet_success_rate, runlet_error_rate_by_type, runlet_latency_p50/p95, runlet_dryrun_diff_rate, telemetry_event_size_distribution. Goal: reduce runbook telemetry noise by 70% and surface three high-value signals to the Console within the first month.

2026-03-14 - Aisha: Decision to ship slimlets without a new DSL is final; will rely on existing admin CLI to compose higher-level flows. Next: add migration playbook and runbook mapping tool.
